title: Projects: threads across devices
why: Threads run on the device placement chooses (Jev's Call B asks for the device whenever more than one qualifies): the start travels through a new hub envelope relay with a durable outbox on the sending device (retried after 10, 20, 40 and then every 60 seconds, delivered in order, deduplicated by id), the chosen device creates the worktree and runs the turns with its own account, thread events and coordinator commands cross devices the same way, a thread's page and actions and every coordinator request are proxied to the device that holds the work, and Move coordinator here takes the coordinator from an offline device or an idle coordinator into a fresh session while the former device hands over at its next assignment check: PJ5 passes as an integration test with a simulated member daemon on the same machine and as two browser journeys in four layouts (8 of 8 in both matrix runs, 12 screenshots), the full backend passed 1515 tests with 4 missing-key skips and 0 failures, and the browser matrix passed 204 of 204 with four workers in both runs, all simulated (no second physical device, scripted and fixture Jev answers, FakeRuntime turns, fake GitHub server) with the vision checks not run at the phase gate without the dedicated Claude token (a builder review of the screenshots found and fixed problems but does not replace them), the brief's two background peer routes deliberately replaced by the relay, and the owner-question fallback for an offline coordinator device, missing at the phase gate, built afterwards on 2026-10-05; see docs/acceptance/PJ5.md. Phase 8 (2026-10-06): the review's fixes give handover envelopes ids that follow the assignment, drop and name a relayed record a member cannot read instead of holding its inbox, and make recovery's relayed event byte-stable; the final backend run passed 1602 tests with 4 missing-key skips and 0 failures and the four-worker browser matrix 208 of 208 on its first run, while PJ-live is blocked without the dedicated Jev, Codex and GitHub credentials; the vision checks of the Projects journeys then passed live on dev-madrid (2026-10-06, at 49106b7: 104 of 104 screenshots ok, 0 blocking findings), and at the final commit 6647f91 the whole browser matrix except installation passed there with all 356 screenshots judged live, 0 blocking findings; see docs/acceptance/REPORT.md.

title: Projects: main isolation with mail and reservations
why: Threads can work directly on main in a device's project checkout when the project's Git policy allows it: placement puts a main thread only on a device whose checkout is on main and free (a busy checkout excludes the device and is never queued), preparation claims the checkout through the conversations' checkout ownership so conversations and other main threads stay off it, publication commits leftovers, verifies, rebases onto origin/main under the publication lease, verifies again and pushes, a conflict gives the thread the brief's exact main-conflict prompt, a stop saves unpublished commits under refs/jevellan/discard, and main threads coordinate through hub-stored advisory path reservations and mail to each other and the coordinator: PJ6 passes as an integration test with two devices and one bare origin (two main threads reserve overlapping paths, exchange mail, publish in turn, and the second resolves a real rebase conflict), beside 9 main publication and 13 mail and reservation cases, the full backend passed 1549 tests with 4 missing-key skips and 0 failures, and the browser matrix passed 204 of 204 with four workers, all simulated (a member daemon on the same machine, scripted Jev answers, test-driven FakeRuntime turns) with the vision checks not run at the phase gate without the dedicated Claude token (phase 6 adds no browser journey; the PJ3 and PJ4b journeys assert Main where it is allowed, and a builder review of the screenshots and probed main-thread pages found and fixed problems but does not replace the vision checks); see docs/acceptance/PJ6.md. Phase 8 (2026-10-06): a main thread never writes to a claimed checkout that is off main, Stop ends a main publication before the push, unsettled checkout claims are settled again at every sweep, and a retried stop gives a checkout the owner worked in back as it is; the final backend run passed 1602 tests with 4 missing-key skips and 0 failures and the four-worker browser matrix 208 of 208 on its first run, while PJ-live is blocked without the dedicated Jev, Codex and GitHub credentials; the vision checks of the Projects journeys then passed live on dev-madrid (2026-10-06, at 49106b7: 104 of 104 screenshots ok, 0 blocking findings), and at the final commit 6647f91 the whole browser matrix except installation passed there with all 356 screenshots judged live, 0 blocking findings; see docs/acceptance/REPORT.md.

title: Projects: terminal takeover

title: Projects: Claude cloud threads
why: Run project threads as Claude cloud sessions as well as on the owner's devices.

title: Projects: browser terminal
why: Take over a thread in a terminal inside the web app, beside jevellan thread attach.

why: Let the coordinator run on a schedule or on its own initiative, not only when an event arrives.

why: Let the coordinator merge pull requests it judges ready instead of leaving every merge to the owner.

why: Notify the owner on their devices when a question is waiting or a pull request is ready.
